_comment: Declared boot-survival contract, consumed by scripts/check-boot-readiness.mjs. OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W1 (SEC-18). Every unit listed here MUST come back on its own after an unplanned reboot (Hetzner maintenance, panic, OOM) — not merely be running today.
_why_effective_enablement: A naive `is-enabled != enabled` check is WRONG and dangerous. Measured on both live hosts at R0: `ssh.service` reports `disabled` because Ubuntu 24.04 socket-activates it (`ssh.socket` is enabled), and `algovault-funnel-snapshot.service` reports `disabled` because its `.timer` is enabled. Both are correct by design, and 'fixing' either would be a real misconfiguration — enabling ssh.service alongside ssh.socket, or making a timer's service run at boot. So each row declares HOW the unit is legitimately activated, and the canary verifies THAT.

_activation_semantics.enabled: the unit itself must be `systemctl is-enabled` = enabled|enabled-runtime
_activation_semantics.socket: the named socket unit must be enabled; the .service is expected to be `disabled`
_activation_semantics.timer: the named timer unit must be enabled; the .service is expected to be `static` or `disabled`

_container_ruling_semantics: Every container LIVE on a host is explicitly RULED ON, in exactly one of two lists, so that boot-contract-canary.sh's `undeclared = live - containers - acknowledged` can reach ZERO and a non-empty undeclared set becomes a real detector instead of a standing complaint (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1). `containers[]` = MUST-SURVIVE: absence after an unattended boot degrades a serving surface, a revenue path, a data producer or a safety control. `acknowledged_containers[]` = ruled NOT boot-critical, WITH A MANDATORY REASON. The reason is MANDATORY: a missing/empty reason is INDETERMINATE, never a silent pass. Exemptions live ON THE ROW and never in prose - an exemption that lives only in a comment gets 'fixed' by a future wave enforcing the contract. (Convention quoted verbatim from ops/monitoring/schedule-boundary-rule.json's `_exemption_semantics`; this is its second application, not a new invention.) A name appearing in BOTH lists is a self-contradiction in a corpus WE author: the parity gate THROWS at build time and the canary reports INDETERMINATE at runtime - 'could not decide', never 'the host drifted'.
_acknowledged_staleness_note: A one-way acknowledged list becomes a stale copy of a world that moved. boot-contract-canary.sh therefore reports `acknowledged_but_absent` as its own positive line when an acknowledged container is no longer live, closing the loop in both directions. Both counts print as explicit zeros on every path - a skipped comparison must never be indistinguishable from a clean one.
_compose_exempt_semantics: `compose_exempt_containers[]` is a BUILD-TIME-ONLY exemption consumed by scripts/check-boot-readiness.mjs R2, which requires every declared container of a `compose_in_this_repo: true` host to appear in THIS repo's committed compose. It is the per-CONTAINER form of the pre-existing per-HOST `compose_in_this_repo: false` exemption, and carries the same mandatory reason. It is deliberately NOT projected to the hosts: the canary verifies restart policy from LIVE `docker inspect`, which is a stronger instrument than a committed-YAML proxy, so this key is not a host decision input and carrying it would only add a field that can drift.
_revisit_rationale: Re-read after any wave that adds or retires a host service. A stale contract silently stops guarding whatever it forgot; if the revisit date passes the canary reports INDETERMINATE rather than a confident pass.
_probed_at_note: 2026-08-28 (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1 R0), superseding 2026-07-31 which was 28 days stale and predated a 7-container drift. WHAT WAS PROBED, on both hosts, read-only: `docker ps` live names + `docker inspect .HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name` for every container (signal-1 6/6, aoe-1 8/8 - all policies within acceptable_restart_policies); both host clocks (`date -u`, agreeing with the operator's machine to 6s); /etc/algovault-host-label on both; the apex Caddy handles for /js/insights.js and /pa/event; aoe-1's cloudflared ingress map; aoe-1:8080 reachability from a peer-host vantage and from the operator's machine; and aoe-supervisor's live SPINE_CONTAINERS / _AOE_CONTAINER_NAME_FILTER source. Units were NOT re-probed this wave - their last live assertion is boot-contract-canary.sh's daily run.

every application container depends on it

signal-1._acknowledged_containers_note: EMPTY BY RULING, not by omission: all 6 containers live on signal-1 at 2026-08-28 are MUST-SURVIVE. The 3 plausible-ce-* rows were promoted from the spec's ACKNOWLEDGED hypothesis by architect ruling (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1 Q1, 2026-08-28) on a probe the hypothesis had not considered: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile serves `handle /js/insights.js` (rewrite -> /js/pa-gfOGxVcQKNfocPr5V3vR8.js) and `handle /pa/event` (rewrite -> /api/event) on the APEX by `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000`, i.e. into plausible-ce-plausible-1. Absence therefore 502s two live algovault.com routes and drops every beacon in the window - the MUST-SURVIVE limb met literally. The route is a DELIBERATE apex dependency created by OPS-PLAUSIBLE-FIRSTPARTY-PROXY-W1 to serve analytics first-party and evade ad-block, not an incidental proxy. The two datastores follow by the app's own declared `depends_on: {plausible_db: service_healthy, plausible_events_db: service_healthy}` in /opt/plausible-ce/compose.yml: with either absent the app container never starts, so both sit on the same apex serving path. Settled by reading depends_on, with nothing stopped in production. Measured live 2026-08-28: /js/insights.js -> 200, apex / -> 200; GET /pa/event -> 404 is CORRECT (it rewrites to Plausible's POST-only /api/event) and is not a defect. Decisive supporting fact: ZERO rows in ops/monitoring/monitoring-inventory.json and ZERO in ops/monitoring/alert-registry.json cover plausible liveness, so acknowledging these would have left no detection at all - and `acknowledged_but_absent` is a REPORT that never reaches send_telegram.sh, so it could not have substituted for one. Once OPS-PLAUSIBLE-ROUTE-SOFTFAIL-W1 makes the two apex handles degrade to 204/404 instead of 502, plausible-ce-plausible-1 may be demoted to acknowledged; until then the promotion IS the detection.

compose_exempt_containers.reason: Plausible CE's compose lives at /opt/plausible-ce/compose.yml (upstream plausible/community-edition) and is not tracked in this repo, so check-boot-readiness.mjs R2 cannot verify its restart policy from committed code. Live policy IS verified on every run by ops/monitoring/boot-contract-canary.sh via `docker inspect .HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name` - measured `always` on 2026-08-28 - which is a stronger instrument than a committed-YAML proxy. Vendoring the compose is REFUSED for the reason OPS-AOE-COMPOSE-BOOT-CONTRACT-W{NEXT} was retired on 2026-08-15: a duplicated fact drifts.

Same exemption and same reason as plausible-ce-plausible-1: compose at /opt/plausible-ce/compose.yml, untracked here; live policy `always` verified by boot-contract-canary.sh via docker inspect on every run.

Same exemption and same reason as plausible-ce-plausible-1: compose at /opt/plausible-ce/compose.yml, untracked here; live policy `always` verified by boot-contract-canary.sh via docker inspect on every run.

aoe-1.compose_exemption_reason: The AOE stack lives in the SEPARATE `autonomous-optimizer` repo and is rsync-deployed to /opt/algovault/autonomous-optimizer (docker-compose.aoe.yml is not tracked here). This repo therefore CANNOT verify its restart policies in code - R2 is reported-but-not-enforced for this host, never silently skipped. WHAT COVERS IT INSTEAD, corrected 2026-08-28 (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1 R4.1): ops/monitoring/boot-contract-canary.sh, shipped by OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W3, reads LIVE `docker inspect` on this host daily and asserts every declared container's actual restart policy. That is a stronger instrument than the committed-YAML proxy the prior pointer promised. The previously-cited tracking wave OPS-AOE-COMPOSE-BOOT-CONTRACT-W{NEXT} was RETIRED on 2026-08-15 and will never exist - it proposed enforcing a committed-YAML proxy instead of live policy, and vendoring another repo's compose creates exactly the duplicated-fact drift CLAUDE.md forbids. Do not re-file it.
aoe-1._nine_vs_four_vs_eight: RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1 R0.2). Three numbers had been attached to this one host and none was wrong; they counted three different things, and the prose above previously carried only the first without saying so. NINE = the containers live on aoe-1 when OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W1 measured it (2026-08-01) - the 8 live today PLUS `autonomous-optimizer-shadow-evaluator-1`. Its `9/9 returned` claim was ACCURATE WHEN WRITTEN: aoe-1's own journal shows shadow-evaluator Removed at 2026-07-31T15:34:28Z with the whole stack, and re-Created at 15:34:49Z after the rehearsal reboot, alongside the other eight. FOUR = the MUST-SURVIVE subset this contract declares in `containers[]`; it was never a live count and was never intended as one. EIGHT = live today, and since 2026-08-01: shadow-evaluator has had zero lifecycle events since that reboot because it sits behind compose `profiles: ['shadow-sim']`, while algovault-aoe.service runs `docker compose -f docker-compose.aoe.yml up -d` with no profile selected, so it is simply never created. Nothing broke; a profile-gated service stopped being activated. shadow-evaluator is therefore deliberately absent from BOTH lists below - listing it as acknowledged would make `acknowledged_but_absent` fire forever, which is the same never-reaches-zero decay this wave exists to retire.

Zero-Trust access to the internal dashboard

acknowledged_containers.reason: Covered by aoe-supervisor's SPINE_CONTAINERS set {aoe-redis, aoe-prefect-server, aoe-prefect-worker, aoe-pg-tunnel}, which is DETECT-ONLY: never auto-restarted (an errant reconcile bouncing the worker on a 2-vCPU box is real blast radius), but paged CRIT once per outage after SPINE_PAGE_AFTER_SECONDS=300 via _send_alert -> _telegram_send. THIS IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM FROM THE PREFIX FILTER that covers the three rows below, and the distinction is load-bearing: `aoe-prefect-worker` does NOT match _AOE_CONTAINER_NAME_FILTER = 'autonomous-optimizer-', so the prefix filter alone would leave the executor of every AOE flow uncovered. Measured 2026-08-28 in the live supervisor container: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID_AOE are both present, so the page path is credentialled - but it has fired zero times in 30 days (no spine outage), so it is committed-and-credentialled and first-invocation-untested. If SPINE detect-only is ever removed or the supervisor demoted, this row must be re-ruled MUST-SURVIVE.

Absence is self-healing via aoe-supervisor's AUTO-RESTART recoverable set, selected by _AOE_CONTAINER_NAME_FILTER = 'autonomous-optimizer-' (deliberately narrow, architect-ratified: OPS-AOE-CHAOS-RECOVERY-W1 Q2(b), 2026-08-02). BOTH LINKS OF THE CHAIN, stated on this row so the blast radius is visible from here alone: the recovering agent is `aoe-supervisor`, and aoe-supervisor is itself declared in this host's containers[] above - so a future wave that DEMOTES or removes aoe-supervisor removes the coverage for this row and the two below, and must re-rule all three. This row REFUTES the spec's own MUST-SURVIVE hypothesis (OPS-BOOT-CONTRACT-WIDEN-W1 R1); it is a real producer (`aoe promotion scan --since 14` every 900s into duckdb-volume), which is why the ruling rests on the recovery mechanism and not on it being inert.

Same AUTO-RESTART mechanism as promotion-scanner: matches _AOE_CONTAINER_NAME_FILTER = 'autonomous-optimizer-', recovered by aoe-supervisor, which is itself declared must-survive above. AND it is on NO serving path, checked explicitly rather than assumed: it publishes 0.0.0.0:8080 inside the box but is UNREACHABLE from a peer-host vantage and from the operator's machine (curl exit 28 both ways, measured 2026-08-28 - the Hetzner Cloud Firewall has suppressed it since OPS-HOST-EXPOSURE-POSTURE-W1 on 2026-07-30, a firewall rule rather than a rebind), and aoe-1's cloudflared ingress maps only aoe.algovault.com -> 127.0.0.1:4200 with everything else -> http_status:404. Internal-ops MCP, not user-facing. If OPS-AOE-MCP-BEHIND-TUNNEL-W{NEXT} ever puts it behind an ingress hostname, that makes it a serving path and this row must be re-ruled.

Same AUTO-RESTART mechanism as promotion-scanner: matches _AOE_CONTAINER_NAME_FILTER = 'autonomous-optimizer-', recovered by aoe-supervisor, which is itself declared must-survive above. Non-producing and on no serving path, checked rather than assumed: it publishes 127.0.0.1:8081 (loopback only, measured via `ss -ltnp`) and aoe-1's cloudflared ingress has no rule for it - the only mapped hostname is aoe.algovault.com -> 127.0.0.1:4200 (aoe-prefect-server, which IS declared must-survive). It renders from duckdb-volume and archive-volume; it writes nothing that is lost by its absence.

_restart_policy_note: `unless-stopped` also means an EXPLICITLY stopped container does NOT auto-start after a boot. So `docker compose stop` before a reboot silently forfeits auto-recovery — recorded here because it is counter-intuitive and was nearly acted on during this wave.
_stop_budget_note: Measured on the real event (OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W1 R2): `shutting down` -> `database system is shut down` took 459 ms, and the restart logged a clean `database system was shut down at ...` with zero crash-recovery markers. The floor here is insurance against future growth, not a live emergency.
